title.narrative: Georgia I2Q - Innovation, Inclusion and Quality

description.narrative: The development objective of the Innovation, Inclusion and Quality Project for Georgia are to (i) expand access to preschool education and (ii) improve the quality of education and learning environments. It has five components. First component, Improving the Quality of and Access to Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) is to provide support to facilitate expanded access to quality pre-school education in selected pre-schools. It has three sub-components. (i) Improving the quality of ECEC programs across the country; ii) Increasing equitable access to preschool education for successful transition to school; and iii) Improving infrastructure to support innovative primary education, including preschool; Second component, Fostering Quality Teaching and Learning in General Education to provide a learning environment that is conducive to quality education in selected general education schools. It has four components. (i) Improving the educational infrastructure to support learning; (ii) Supporting the scaling up of the whole-school improvement pilot; iii) Supporting the capacity-building of teachers and school leaders (principals) to adapt, develop, and implement school-based curriculum; and (iv) Assisting the development of a national assessment framework; Third component, Strengthening Financing Options and Promoting Internationalization in Higher Education is to improve the quality and international competitiveness of higher education. It has four sub-components.(i) Developing new options for higher education financing, including performance-based options to support the Government's strategic objective; (ii) Establishment of a Competitive Innovation Fund (CIF) for public and private universities, in partnership with private sector; (iii) Promoting internationalization of higher education; and (iv) Strengthening the quality of pre-service teacher education programs for all levels of education; Fourth component, System Strengthening and Stakeholder Communication is to facilitate a shift in attitude toward learning in Georgia to one that is more pro-active, student-centered, innovative, and evidence-based; It has two sub-components. i) Supporting data-driven decision-making accessible to the entire education system and ii) Communication and stakeholder consultations for education reform; Fifth component, Supporting Project Management, Monitoring, and Evaluations is to support capacity-building for effective management of proposed project. It has one sub-component. (i) Facilitating the establishment, staffing, and evaluation of project operations will support the day-to-day management and monitoring of the proposed project through the establishment and maintenance of a Project Management Unit (PMU) under the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport (MESCS) and maintaining adequate capacity in the Municipal Development Fund of Georgia (MDF) under the Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure.
The project development objectives are to (i) expand access to preschool education and (ii) improve the quality of education and learning environments.

title.narrative: Performance-based funding model for higher education institutions and its administration tools developed

comment.narrative: As of November 10, 2025, 75% of the work is completed. The performance-based funding (PBF) model was delivered through Progress Report 4, verified by MoESY and the steering group. For the pilot system, the consultant introduced the pilot module, updated user manual, and system specifications. IMDS pilot v4.0 will be refined following MESY and EMIS feedback. For the legal documentation, the consultant submitted preliminary draft implementation instructions on October 23, 2025. These will be refined and finalized in Progress Report 6 (due January 31, 2026).

title.narrative: Performance-based funding model for higher education institutions and its administration tools developed

comment.narrative: On track: The model has been successfully developed and approved by the MoESY, with its submission included in the 4th Report from the Consultant, officially approved on November 26, 2024. Efforts are currently focused on preparing a package of regulatory legislative changes for establishing the legal framework necessary for the Performance-based funding model's implementation. Once finalized, this package of amendments will also be submitted to the MoESY. Concurrently, work is ongoing to develop a higher education funding management system. A pilot version has been created and is available for testing by both the MoESY and EMIS.

On track: This indicator measures the status and progress towards the development of a merit-based scholarship model.
On track: The model has been successfully developed and accepted by the MoESY, with its submission included in the 4th Report from the Consultant, officially approved on November 26, 2024. Efforts are currently focused on preparing a package of regulatory legislative changes for establishing the legal framework necessary for the merit-based scholarship model's implementation.

title.narrative: Performance-based funding model for higher education institutions and its administration tools developed

comment.narrative: The performance-based funding (PBF) model was delivered through Progress Report 4, verified by MoESY and the steering group. For the pilot system, the consultant introduced the pilot module, updated user manual, and system specifications. IMDS pilot v4.0 will be refined following MESY and EMIS feedback. For the legal documentation, the consultant submitted preliminary draft implementation instructions on October 23, 2025. These will be refined and finalized in Progress Report 6.

title.narrative: Merit-based student grant system developed acceptable for the MoESY.

comment.narrative:
Achieved: Merit-based student grant system and the set of legislative changes required to implement the revised grant system for higher education have been developed.
The merit-based grant system was delivered through Progress Report 4, verified by MESY and the contract steering group, and formally submitted via official correspondence No. 1520070 dated November 26, 2024, in the Ministry's document management system (E-Flow). The comprehensive legislative amendment package (16 legal and sublegal acts) was delivered through Progress Report 5, verified by MESY and the contract steering group, and formally submitted via official correspondence No. 933884 dated July 31, 2025, in the Ministry's document management system (E-Flow).

title.narrative: Performance-based funding model for higher education institutions and its administration tools developed

comment.narrative: Achieved: This indicator covered three workstreams — developing a PBF model (40%), deploying PBF modules into the IMDS pilot system (40%), and establishing the legal basis for IMDS (20%) — all of which have been fully delivered. The PBF model was completed and verified in late 2024. The IMDS pilot system (version 4.2 UAT), delivered in February 2026, includes a KPI catalogue, funding logic, and tools for MESY to assign KPIs, weights, and tranches to individual HEIs, with a dedicated portal for HEI-level tracking and reporting. A demonstration session with senior MESY leadership took place in March 2026. The system also integrates SIEM and SSO capabilities. The legal framework — a draft Ministerial Order on the rules for administering the higher education financing system — was delivered and formally submitted to MESY in February 2026.
